- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for 30d horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be closer to recent 7–14 day average, not extrapolated trend.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent auction events; dampen forecast by 5–10% if event count >15/30d.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish → bearish transitions, model fails to adjust; apply lagged correction: subtract 1–2% for each 3-day lag after bullish sentiment peak.
